newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Skoda to build two plants in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Skoda to build two plants in Brazil.

text.p: Czech truck maker Skoda plans to build two plants costing $150 million each in Brazil, said a spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.

She said that Skoda vice-president Wladimir Knezek had told Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles that one plant will be in the southern state of Santa Catarina, producing 5,000 units per year within three years.
The other plant will be built in the northeastern state of Bahia and will build specialized trucks for the mining industry.
"Skoda intends to make of Brazil a major launchpad for exports to Latin America and Asia," the spokeswoman quoted Dornelles as saying. Work on the factories should begin in 1998.
The plant in Bahia will benefit from special fiscal incentives granted to carmakers who establish themselves in the northeast or the interior of Brazil.
